page: Microsoft Azure D32nlds_v6 is a network-optimized virtual machine within the Dnldv6 family, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes no GPU acceleration hardware.

Local ephemeral storage is provided via 1,890 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, offering low-latency scratch space for I/O-heavy operations. The system is also compatible with Azure Premium Storage for external managed disk attachments. Networking features are optimized for throughput, and the virtual machine is deployed without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on virtual network interfaces for external connectivity.

By adopting a constrained memory profile relative to core count, the server reduces hardware overhead for applications that require sustained multi-core processing without large in-memory caches. The high NVMe storage capacity paired with 32 execution threads provides balanced performance for parallel compute tasks that regularly read and write local files.

Primary workload targets include batch compute pipelines, software build environments, continuous integration workers, network virtual appliances, and intermediate data transformation jobs that rely on fast local disk access.
description: The Microsoft Azure D32nlds_v6 is a virtual machine within the Dnldv6 family, designed for network-optimized and compute-focused workloads requiring lower memory density. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance features 32 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs backed by an Intel processor and is paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is anchored by 1,890 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD capacity, alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include GPU acceleration and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By reducing the memory-to-core ratio compared to traditional general-purpose offerings, the D32nlds_v6 offers a cost-effective hardware footprint for compute-centric tasks that benefit from fast local temporary disk I/O without incurring memory overhead. It is well suited for batch data processing, network virtual appliances, CI/CD worker nodes, and scalable web application backends.
